10.1002/cjce.70020: Hardwood charcoal held beeswax to form a heat-storage material. The composite stored **77.83 J/g as latent heat**, with no performance loss over 20 tested cycles. Wax uptake reached 61.2%. Similar uptake was reported when particle size increased from millimetres to centimetres; longer cycling was not established by these tests.
10.1002/cjce.25755: A potassium-promoted nickel catalyst on ordered porous alumina converted **85% of CO₂ at 450°C and atmospheric pressure**. Conversion reached 94% at 9 atm under the reported flow conditions. A separate 150-hour test at 300°C showed no loss of activity, at a lower conversion of 38%.
10.1002/cjce.25720: Fungal pellets were tested for removing persistent benzotriazole compounds from domestic wastewater. Chlorobenzotriazole removal averaged **70% ± 17%**, compared with 62% ± 16% in the control. Removal of several other tested compounds was 17–19%, while the control removed none of those compounds.
10.1002/cjce.25751: The study compared three microbial electrochemical systems for treating oil-sands process water. At a **2.4-day retention time**, the electrolysis cell removed 79% of organic material, compared with 4.0% in the fuel cell. Increasing the applied voltage to 2 V raised naphthenic-acid removal to 70%.
10.1002/cjce.25749: Surfactants extracted from tea plants were compared for oil recovery. Modified saponin lowered oil–water interfacial tension to **0.375 mN/m at 1,125 ppm**, compared with 7.582 mN/m for the crude extract at its optimum concentration. Flooding with modified saponin increased recovery by 15.8% of the original oil in place in the reported tests.
10.1002/cjce.25770: Waste cooking oil was converted to biodiesel using a catalyst made from blast-furnace slag. The reported optimum yield was **98.635%**, at about 57.5°C after 6.7 hours. Catalyst reuse still needs testing.
10.1002/cjce.70004: The study compared mechanical recycling and heat-driven recovery of acrylic plastic. After five injection-moulding cycles, impact strength and optical quality had deteriorated substantially. A silicon-carbide bed recovered **92% methyl methacrylate monomer**; the cracking catalyst instead produced unwanted products and coke.
10.1002/cjce.70011: A simpler equation predicts when natural-gas hydrates dissociate. It was checked against **1,879 measurements** for seven hydrate-forming gases, over 0.093–493 MPa. Average absolute temperature error was 0.25 K; average relative pressure error was 2.82%.
10.1002/cjce.70181: The model represents heating and cooling equipment as a network that can suffer multiple failures. In the two example systems, correctly sized thermal storage enabled **100% of demand to be met** within the model's cost constraints. This is a modelling result, not a guarantee for an operating plant.
10.1002/cjce.70184: Electrospinning uses an electric field to draw a polymer solution into fine fibres. Fibre shape depends on the solution, feed rate, voltage and collector spacing. This review identifies three remaining needs: industrial scale-up guidance, safer solvents and better models for choosing operating conditions.
10.1002/cjce.70032: This review covers AI for process control, fault detection, maintenance and energy use. Its main implementation limits are poor data, computing demands, connections to older systems and models that are difficult to explain. It reviews applications rather than reporting a new plant trial.
10.1002/cjce.70038: An algorithm updates models that estimate how many operating cycles remain in gas-dehydration beds. Logistic models performed best for beds lasting at least as long as the reference bed; a Bayesian method did better for shorter-lived beds. The algorithm was integrated into an **offshore plant's live monitoring dashboard**.
10.1002/cjce.70080: Neural differential-equation models learned hydrocracking behaviour from **synthetic data**. Prediction error stayed below 0.5 wt.% under most conditions inside the training range. Accuracy fell when predicting higher temperatures outside that range, especially for the more nonlinear reaction model.
10.1002/cjce.70095: Mild heat treatment increased the energy content per unit mass of some waste materials by **up to 1.73 times**. Reported energy recovery ranged from 69.3% to 99.15%. Lemon peel gave the largest increase in energy density; paper cups retained the most energy. Results depended on waste type, temperature and gas atmosphere.
10.1002/cjce.70092: A process model estimates hydrogen production by splitting natural gas with plasma. At commercially relevant conditions, predicted electricity demand was **20.12 kWh per kg of hydrogen**, compared with 21.54 kWh/kg reported for an industrial facility. The model was checked against laboratory data before being scaled up in simulation.
10.1002/cjce.70070: A zinc–air battery removed salt while generating electricity. Salt rejection was **98.5% at 2,500 ppm NaCl**, falling to 59.7% at 7,500 ppm. Higher feed salinity reduced performance. Oxygen nanobubbles improved rejection by about 12% in the reported tests.
10.1002/cjce.25693: This review examines biochar for removing cadmium, chromium, lead and nickel from water. Feedstock, heating conditions and surface treatment determine adsorption behaviour. It also covers regeneration, reuse, cost and life-cycle impacts; it does not establish one best material for every wastewater.
10.1002/cjce.70079: The review examines biorefineries that combine biological and heat-based processes to use more of each biomass feedstock. It covers routes to fuels, gases and solid products, including reuse of by-products. Pretreatment, supply chains and compatibility between processes remain central design requirements.
10.1002/cjce.70015: For tall oil from kraft pulping, the optimized process gave a **52.9 wt.% crude-oil yield**. Adding 0.018 wt.% anionic processing aid raised the yield to 57.1 wt.%. The baseline conditions included pH 2.5–3.0, 90–100°C, a 20-minute reaction and two hours of settling.
10.1002/cjce.70094: An automated solvent-extraction method measured oil-sand composition and cleaned the solids. Extraction took **5–60 minutes**, depending on the sample. Paired tests gave equivalent bitumen and solids measurements to the conventional Dean–Stark method, while reducing manual handling and solvent exposure.
10.1002/cjce.70132: This review compares lithium recovery from brines, minerals and waste. It focuses on making lithium carbonate and lithium hydroxide pure enough for battery materials. Separation of other dissolved ions, product purity, environmental impact and scale-up determine whether a recovery route is useful.
10.1002/cjce.70151: The review follows lignin from biomass extraction through nanoparticle production and chemical modification. Smaller particles provide more surface area and reactive sites. Proposed uses include UV protection, antimicrobial materials and emulsion stabilization; the article reviews routes and applications rather than one new performance test.
10.1002/cjce.25363: A cobalt complex supported on activated carbon was tested for removing methylene blue from water. Model-based optimization predicted **99.56% removal** at 9.36 mg/L dye, 15.72 mg adsorbent and 311.2 K. This maximum is an optimization result; the abstract does not establish performance on real mixed wastewater.
10.1002/cjce.70174: This review examines electrochemical lithium recovery from brine and seawater. It compares electrolysis, electrodialysis and capacitive methods, including changes to electrodes and membranes to improve selectivity. Moving from laboratory and pilot systems to industrial scale remains a major challenge.
10.1002/cjce.70345: A career article describes moving from a faculty position into academic administration. Based partly on the author's experience as a director, it discusses service, leadership and working across disciplines. These are practical observations and personal views, rather than results from a controlled study.
10.1002/cjce.70186: The study tested how salt changes the behaviour of surfactant-coated silica and alumina particles at an oil–water boundary. Interfacial tension reached its minimum at **25,000 ppm salinity** in the tested systems. Coating type also changed aggregation and the speed at which the interface reached equilibrium.
10.1002/cjce.70211: This review examines joining small olefin molecules into diesel-range products using ZSM-5 catalysts. Catalysts with pores at different scales can improve transport through the material. It also considers olefin-rich refinery streams as feedstocks and changes to refinery operation; it does not report a new commercial production run.
10.1002/cjce.70235: With conventional alum, nanoplastic removal fell below **20% above pH 7.8**. Under these higher-pH conditions, aluminium chlorohydrate plus pDADMAC averaged 66% nanoplastic removal. Aluminium chlorohydrate averaged 94% microfibre removal. Water chemistry and settling time affected the results.
10.1002/cjce.70374: The article uses **three anonymized accounts** from chemical engineering to examine academic bullying and group harassment. It links these experiences to published research and discusses the role of unequal power and silent bystanders. Its proposed responses include enforceable conduct rules and systematic data collection; the accounts are not a prevalence estimate.
10.1002/cjce.70198: A reaction model describes styrene–butyl acrylate emulsion polymerization in batch and 3D-printed tubular reactors. The initiating system can operate at **25°C** and produce latex particles as small as 35 nm. Predictions broadly matched experiments; non-ideal flow may explain differences during continuous operation.
10.1002/cjce.70225: A hybrid flotation column added mechanical mixing to a conventional column. In **air–water tests at 1,500 rpm**, it held more gas while maintaining similar bubble-size distributions. Improved fine-particle recovery is a proposed application; ore recovery was not measured in these two-phase tests.
10.1002/cjce.70297: Four learning models were tested on **154 crude-distillation simulation records**. The neural network performed best, with R² = 0.9742. The data came from Aspen HYSYS simulations of three crude oils, so this result does not establish accuracy on independent operating-plant data.
10.1002/cjce.70290: Adding geopolymer and zeolite to polymer fibres changed their strength and gas uptake. Hydrogen uptake increased from **0.01 to 0.08 mmol/g** for the reported MZ30 membrane. Carbon dioxide uptake did not show the same improvement: measured values remained close to or below those of the plain polymer.
10.1002/cjce.70304: The proposed experiment-design method accounts for uncertainty in inputs, such as the starting reactant concentration. In simulations of a batch pharmaceutical process, it estimated model parameters more accurately than a method that assumed exact inputs. The comparison used repeated random simulations, not a reported plant trial.
10.1002/cjce.70276: The process precipitates niobic acid and heats it to make niobium oxide. Reducing the washing solids-to-liquid ratio from 60 to 20 g/L lowered residual potassium **threefold, to 0.06 wt.%**. This prevented the unwanted potassium–niobium oxide phases observed at higher potassium levels.
10.1002/cjce.70355: Models used historical pilot-furnace data to estimate sidewall temperature and molten-bath size between tapping cycles. Reported percentage errors were **0.29% for temperature** and 9.5% for bath size. The work supports monitoring of wall protection; it does not demonstrate that all molten-material leaks can be prevented.
10.1002/cjce.70342: Porous fibres released mixed insect pheromones for possible use in protective crop nets. Peak component release rates were **11–189 mg/m²/day**, above the stated minimum dose of 0.05–0.09 mg/m²/day. Release depended mainly on volatility. Peak rates alone do not establish how long effective release lasts.
10.1002/cjce.70307: In steam-assisted bitumen-recovery experiments, uniformly dispersed iron-oxide nanoparticles at **1,000 ppm produced 83% oil recovery**. The particles retained asphaltenes, and the recovered oil had lower viscosity. Both particle placement and concentration mattered; the result comes from experiments rather than a field deployment.
10.1002/cjce.70320: Simulated pressure-swing adsorption used **0.30 MJ/kg of syngas**, compared with 15.31 MJ/kg for amine absorption. The trade-off was purity: 83.91% versus 97.21%. The comparison used a Brazilian economic and environmental context; lower energy demand did not mean equal product purity.
10.1002/cjce.70500: Magnetometry measures a material's magnetic response and can track catalyst phases during operation. A key limit is that strong magnetic phases can hide weaker signals. Because the measurement covers the whole sample, separating contributions from several phases is difficult.
10.1002/cjce.70497: This editorial defines the responsibilities of peer reviewers. It argues against forced self-citation, demands that unnecessarily expand a study, and replacing expert judgement with language-model output. Its practical distinction is simple: reviewers advise; editors make the decision.
10.1002/cjce.70505: This introduction covers synthetic jet fuel that must work with existing aircraft engines and airport infrastructure. Topics include alcohol-to-jet and Fischer–Tropsch routes, fuel-property checks and the effect of olefins on heat and oxidation stability. This summary is based on the publisher's Issue Highlights page.
10.1002/cjce.70383: This review maps AI methods used to predict enzyme behaviour, stability and solubility. Its main limits are the shortage of high-quality data and poor transfer of models between enzyme classes. It is a review of the research landscape, not a new demonstration of an AI-designed enzyme.
